# google_cloud_identity_inbound_oidc_sso_profile

An OIDC federation between a Google enterprise customer and an OIDC identity provider.

The caller must be a Google Workspace / Cloud Identity administrator of the
customer with the SSO settings privilege (for example a super admin);
Google Cloud IAM roles are not sufficient.

If you are using User ADCs (Application Default Credentials) with this resource,
you must specify a `billing_project` and set `user_project_override` to true
in the provider configuration. Otherwise the Cloud Identity API will return a 403 error.
Your account must have the `serviceusage.services.use` permission on the
`billing_project` you defined.


To get more information about InboundOidcSsoProfile, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/identity/docs/reference/rest/v1/inboundOidcSsoProfiles)
* How-to Guides
    * [Assign SSO profiles](https://cloud.google.com/identity/docs/how-to/assign-sso-profiles)
    * [Set up SSO with OIDC](https://support.google.com/a/answer/13511217)

~> **Warning:** If the customer has Multi-Party Approval (MPA) enabled for sensitive actions, creating, updating, or deleting an SSO profile returns an operation awaiting second-admin approval (`awaiting-multi-party-approval`) and Terraform will return an error until the request is approved in Google Admin Console (after approval, a newly created profile can be imported or an updated profile refreshed).

~> **Warning:** All arguments including the following potentially sensitive
values will be stored in the raw state as plain text: `rp_config.client_secret`.
[Read more about sensitive data in state](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/manage-sensitive-data).


## Example Usage - Cloud Identity Inbound Oidc Sso Profile Basic


```hcl
resource "google_cloud_identity_inbound_oidc_sso_profile" "oidc_profile" {
  customer     = "customers/A01b123xz"
  display_name = "oidc-profile"

  idp_config {
    issuer_uri          = "https://idp.example.com"
    change_password_uri = "https://idp.example.com/change-password"
  }

  rp_config {
    client_id     = "test-client-id"
    client_secret = "test-client-secret"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `idp_config` -
  (Required)
  OIDC identity provider configuration.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_idp_config).


* `customer` -
  (Optional)
  The customer. For example: `customers/C0123abc`. If omitted, the customer of the caller is used.

* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  Human-readable name of the OIDC SSO profile.

* `rp_config` -
  (Optional)
  OIDC relying party (RP) configuration for this OIDC SSO profile. These are the RP details
  provided by Google that should be configured on the corresponding identity provider.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_rp_config).

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_idp_config"></a>The `idp_config` block supports:

* `issuer_uri` -
  (Required)
  The Issuer identifier for the IdP. Must be a URL. The discovery URL will be derived
  from this as described in Section 4 of the OIDC specification.

* `change_password_uri` -
  (Optional)
  The **Change Password URL** of the identity provider. Users will be sent to this URL
  when changing their passwords at `myaccount.google.com`. This takes precedence over
  the change password URL configured at customer-level. Must use `HTTPS`.

<a name="nested_rp_config"></a>The `rp_config` block supports:

* `client_id` -
  (Optional)
  OAuth2 client ID for OIDC. Must be set together with `client_secret`.

* `client_secret` -
  (Optional)
  Input only. OAuth2 client secret for OIDC. Must be set together with `client_id`.
  **Note**: This property is sensitive and will not be displayed in the plan.

* `redirect_uris` -
  (Output)
  The URL(s) that this client may use in authentication requests.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `inboundOidcSsoProfiles/{{inbound_oidc_sso_profile_id}}`

* `inbound_oidc_sso_profile_id` -
  The server-assigned ID of the OIDC SSO profile (the last segment of `name`).

* `name` -
  Resource name of the OIDC SSO profile, in the format `inboundOidcSsoProfiles/{inbound_oidc_sso_profile_id}`.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


InboundOidcSsoProfile can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `inboundOidcSsoProfiles/{{inbound_oidc_sso_profile_id}}`
* `{{inbound_oidc_sso_profile_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import InboundOidcSsoProfile using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    inboundOidcSsoProfileId = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_cloud_identity_inbound_oidc_sso_profile.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import InboundOidcSsoProfile using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "inboundOidcSsoProfiles/{{inbound_oidc_sso_profile_id}}"
  to = google_cloud_identity_inbound_oidc_sso_profile.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), InboundOidcSsoProfile can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_cloud_identity_inbound_oidc_sso_profile.default inboundOidcSsoProfiles/{{inbound_oidc_sso_profile_id}}
$ terraform import google_cloud_identity_inbound_oidc_sso_profile.default {{inbound_oidc_sso_profile_id}}
```
